1. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT REGARDING TESTIMONY
Q. Please describe the nature of your testimony.

A. | submit this testimony as a landowner pro se intervenor with personal knowledge of
my property and the conditions that would be directly affected by the proposed 765 kV
transmission line.

My testimony is based on my personai observations, firsthand knowledge, and direct
experience regarding my property, including its use, infrastructure, water resources,
wildlife habitat, and planned future residential use.

To the extent | offer opinions, those opinions are rationally based on my firsthand
knowledge and are offered as permissible lay opinion testimony under Texas Rule of
Evidence 701.

To the extent | reference publicly available studies, agency reports, legislative materials,
scientific literature, or statements by others, those references are offered solely to
explain the basis of my concerns and understanding of potential impacts. | am not
offering expert testimony under Texas Rule of Evidence 702.

My testimony is relevant under Texas Rules of Evidence 401 and 402 because it
addresses direct impacts to my property.

Road, Salado, Texas 76571.

My current residence is 5838 St Charles Drive, Belton, Texas 76513.

A. Yes, a pro se Intervenor.

A. | am a husband, father of four growing children, lifelong Texan, and active-duty U.S.
Army Colonel with 23 years of military service of which several years were combat
deployments. | am a Eagle Scout as well.

Wildlife Biologists identified areas they indicated may constitute potential Golden-
cheeked Warbler habitat and confirmed Vermillion Flycatchers. (Exhibits 22, 23, 39)

The proposed project may fragment wildlife habitat and require the removal of native
vegetation and mature tree cover that provide important forage, shelter, and migratory

environmental reports regarding mechanical vegetation reduction and land clearing
further indicate potential secondary impacts to soil stability, erosion, sediment
displacement, stormwater runoff, and altered water flow-through characteristics,
warranting evaluation of applicable mitigation measures and alternative
recommendations identified by the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department.
